transcript: Tonight, I attended the first preview of life of Pi on Broadway. It can be really hard to make stage adaptations for works that were first books or movies, but this adaptation leans heavily into its design elements to make for a really immersive viewing experience that doesn't try to replicate the movie. It's quite original. It's visually mesmerizing with so many surprises throughout the entire production. It's theatrical, it's playful, it's really artfully done, especially the puppetry. Often the actors performing with puppets actually make the sounds of the animals they're portraying, which I thought was really fun. I think depending on how much you're attached to the book of the movie, the script might feel a little underwhelming. But I think it's hard to fully capture all the themes, such as faith in religion, grief, and truth versus relativity in a play that's just over 2 hours long. Especially when a lot of the time and attention is paid toward creating these lush, immersive action scenes that, to me, are the hallmarks of this production. And through these scenes, the large ensemble of actors creates this visual world of the story with as much precision and passion as they exemplify when performing their lines. After the curtain call tonight, we got to recognize the Broadway debuts made with this first preview, and there were so many, so it was really special to get to celebrate that moment with them with that. Another playable for my collection.
